title: Perf: perfkit hotspots on large Chrome traces
description: perfkit hotspots on browser traces is slow and memory-hungry: a 134 MB Playwright trace takes ~1.8 s / 0.8 GB RSS, a 527 MB one ~9 s / 2.5 GB. Metric: wall median of 'perfkit hotspots <trace> --top 15' (stdout to /dev/null); secondary: peak RSS, identical stdout. Workload: .perf/hotspots-trace/inputs/main.trace.json (134 MB, sha256 03271c82f02a8b4e). Hold-out: 527 MB trace (sha256 fb6fe80a8cfdcfeb), not tuned on. Target: as fast as evidence allows within 4 experiments. Rigor: R3 (no test-policy.toml). Real-example campaign for PSKI-12 (Quest+lore integration).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Target met or a stop rule recorded, confirmed on the hold-out trace
tests/ green and hotspot output identical on both traces
Every experiment recorded as a task note with its numbers
Lore perf report linked from this task

implementationNotes: Harness fix (not a perf experiment): hotspot ties were printed in set() order, which varies with PYTHONHASHSEED, so two runs of identical code differed. Fixed (dict.fromkeys + frame-name tie-break) with a regression test; incumbent re-copied; equivalence harness now identical on both traces.

perf E1 [kept] json raw_decode 74.7% self (max x3.95): decode only trace lines load_chrome_trace uses (ProfileChunk, thread_name, X events); expect ~2.5x and <50% RSS -> profiles.load: streaming one-event-per-line pass with full-parse fallback; improved -33.1% (ratio CI 0.664-0.673, p=0.008, n=[10, 10]); guard: 43 tests passed; equiv.sh identical on main and holdout; RSS 785->162 MB (x4.86); gain below prediction -> re-profile

perf E2 [kept] line-filter genexpr+any ~33% (cProfile, inflated): one compiled bytes-regex search per line instead of 4 Python substring tests; expect ~1.2x -> _TRACE_KEEP as compiled regex; improved -20.2% (ratio CI 0.790-0.805, p=0.0025, n=[12, 12]); guard: 43 tests passed; equiv.sh identical on main and holdout

perf E3 [kept] json.loads wrappers (decode+loads+detect_encoding ~13%): module-level JSONDecoder.raw_decode on decoded text skips loads() per-call overhead; expect ~1.08x -> _JSON.raw_decode(line.decode()); improved -12.2% (ratio CI 0.859-0.891, p=0.0029, n=[15, 15]); guard: 43 tests passed; equiv.sh identical on main and holdout

perf E4 [kept] file iteration (line reads across a 134 MB file): 1 MiB read buffer cuts read syscalls; expect ~3% -> open(path, 'rb', buffering=1<<20); improved -5.7% (ratio CI 0.937-0.961, p=0.00073, n=[15, 15]); guard: 43 tests passed; equiv.sh identical on main and holdout; iteration cap (4) reached

Scope change: experiment cap raised from 4 to 5, once, to run E5 (a low-ceiling idea whose expected gain is near the minimum effect) so the rejection path is exercised on a real campaign. Recorded before measuring E5; prediction for E5: ~1-2%, likely below the 2% minimum effect.

perf E5 [reverted] regex search per line 20.3% self: check the commonest kept marker with a bytes 'in' before the regex; expect ~1-2% (likely below threshold) -> b'"ph":"X"' in line or _TRACE_KEEP.search(line); regressed +9.3% (ratio CI 1.076-1.097, p=0.0098, n=[15, 15]); guard: 43 tests passed; equiv.sh identical; REGRESSED +9.3%: the extra Python-level test runs on every line and 77% of lines don't match, costing more than the regex calls it saves. Don't retry without restructuring the scan.
finalSummary: perfkit hotspots on a 134 MB Chrome trace: 1.23 s -> 0.53 s (x2.34, CI 0.427-0.434), RSS 785 -> 162 MB, output identical; hold-out x1.43. 5 experiments, E5 rejected (+9.3%). Report: reference/perf-report-perfkit-hotspots-on-large-chrome-traces. Delivered in feat/PSKI-14-release-v0.1.0.
